data.description:
## Context / Problem

VERIFIED on origin/main @ 144bb02251, by reading the two lines together rather than either alone.

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:106`

    decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)

has NO `errored` guard, and `parity.py:32` defines

    _DECISIONS = ("block", "advisory", "dropped")

`errored` IS computed two lines earlier (`err1, err2 = _rate(v1, ...), _rate(v2, ...)` at :102) and is
therefore available — it is simply not used to exclude a pair from the flip count.

## Why this matters, and why it is worse than a normal false positive

A transient provider error (a throttle, a 5xx, a timeout) on ONE side of the paired run yields a
different `decision` on that side. Because `dropped` is itself a member of `_DECISIONS`, the affected
pair stays in `gold_pairs` and the difference is counted as a DECISION FLIP.

The comment directly above `_DECISIONS` states the stakes: "a FLIP between these on the gold set is
never acceptable (it changes what ships)". So the metric treated as never-acceptable is the one a
transient network event can fabricate.

The error direction is the damaging one. Story S6 (0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac) exists to decide whether
Bedrock CLEARS the parity bar. A fabricated flip fails the Bedrock slot and attributes a transient
infrastructure event to a MODEL QUALITY REGRESSION — so the epic could conclude "Bedrock is not at
parity" on evidence that says nothing about Bedrock quality. It is also silent: the report shows a
flip, not an error, and nothing distinguishes them.

An errored pair should be marked INVALID and excluded from the flip count, not scored as a flip.

## What is NOT established

Whether an errored result actually resolves its `decision` to `dropped` in practice, or to something
outside `_DECISIONS` (in which case the pair leaves `gold_pairs` and the bug does not fire). Check
that FIRST, by constructing an errored result and observing its decision — not by reading. If it
resolves outside `_DECISIONS`, this is a latent hazard rather than a live bug and should be
reclassified, not silently closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] It is established by experiment, not by reading, what `decision` an errored result carries, and
      therefore whether the pair remains in `gold_pairs`.
- [ ] A test constructs a paired run where exactly one side errored and asserts the pair is treated as
      INVALID rather than counted in `decision_flips`; it fails before the fix.
- [ ] The parity report distinguishes an errored/invalid pair from a genuine decision flip in its
      output, so a reader cannot mistake one for the other.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
data.title: parity decision_flips counts a transient error as a decision flip, so one throttle fails the Bedrock parity slot as a quality regression
